featureRef: 4.18 Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals
name: Open the books and read them, tracing any entry back to what caused it
priorityReason: Every other financial use case posts here. Without a way to read the books nobody can prove they are right.

goal.capability: to read the general ledger, the trial balance and the journals, and trace an entry back to its source
goal.outcome: the books can be proved right rather than merely believed, and any figure can be explained

secondaryActors.involvement: Reviews the financial position at summary level.

additional.description: An invoice, payment, correction or voucher posts an entry, which appears here immediately.

preconditions.condition: A chart of accounts exists. No feature in the document creates one, and nothing here can be read without it (BR-1).

establishedBy.name: Accounting vouchers for money in and out

preconditions.condition: Entries have been posted by the use cases that cause them.

establishedBy.name: Issuing fee invoices at different scopes

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Accounts, School Admin or Principal.
A financial year is defined, which the ledger runs against and which is not the academic session (BR-10).

postConditions: The reader has the position of any account over any date range, with a running balance.
The trial balance has been produced and its two columns agree, which is what proves the books are not quietly wrong.
Any entry can be traced to the voucher or invoice that caused it, and from there to the student, supplier or payment behind it.
Nothing has been created, changed or deleted. Reading the books is a read, and there is no screen here that posts an entry.
A figure quoted from the trial balance carries the moment it was produced, so a number read in a meeting can be dated.
Where the two columns do not agree, the difference is shown rather than hidden, since that is the one thing this use case exists to reveal.
Every entry read carries both its sides, so where the money came from and where it went are both visible.

businessRules.rule: The books are read against a chart of accounts. No feature in this document creates one, and it must exist before anything here can be built or read.

Every amount is recorded twice, once for where it came from and once for where it went. The two sides must always total the same, which is what makes it possible to prove the books are not quietly wrong.
The trial balance proves the two columns agree. Where they do not, the difference is shown rather than hidden, because that is the one thing this use case exists to reveal.
Nothing is posted here. Entries arrive because something else happened — an invoice raised, a payment recorded, a correction made, or a voucher entered by hand.
No entry is ever edited or deleted. A correction is a voucher or one of the reversal use cases, never a change to a line in the ledger.
Every entry can be traced to what caused it, and from there to the student, supplier or payment behind it. An entry nobody can trace is an entry nobody can defend.
The ledger shows a running balance in date order, so an account's position at any point in the period is readable without arithmetic.
Every figure carries the moment it was produced. A trial balance quoted in a meeting an hour later has to be datable.
A closed period is readable but not postable. Reading history is always permitted; changing it is not.
The ledger runs against a financial year, which is not necessarily the academic session and is defined nowhere in this document.
Reading the ledger or the trial balance is written to the audit log, because these carry the school's whole financial position.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the account list and selects an account.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Lists the accounts with their type and current balance.

basicFlow.userAction: Views the general ledger for that account over a date range.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows every entry in date order with its debit, its credit and a running balance.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the trial balance as at a date.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Totals both columns and shows whether they agree, with the moment the figure was produced.

basicFlow.userAction: Drills from a trial balance line down to the account.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Opens that account's ledger for the same period.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the entry to see the voucher behind it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows both sides of the posting and what caused it.

basicFlow.userAction: Traces through to the invoice, payment or voucher that caused the entry.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Opens the source document, and from there the student, supplier or payment behind it.

basicFlow.userAction: Reads the journals for the period.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Lists every posting with both its accounts, its amount and who posted it.

alternateFlows.condition: The two columns do not agree
alternateFlows.behaviour: The difference is shown at the top rather than hidden, and the entries that could not be paired are listed. This is the only condition the trial balance exists to reveal (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The reader needs a period from a closed financial year
alternateFlows.navigation: Chart of accounts → General ledger → Date range
alternateFlows.behaviour: The closed period is read normally. Reading history is always permitted; posting into it is not (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The entry arose from a fee invoice
alternateFlows.behaviour: The trace runs through the invoice to the student it was raised against, so a ledger figure resolves to a person.

alternateFlows.condition: The entry arose from a hand-entered voucher
alternateFlows.behaviour: The trace ends at the voucher, which carries its own description and approval. That is the manual door into this ledger (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal wants the position across branches
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Finance → Trial balance → All branches
alternateFlows.behaviour: The trial balance is produced across branches, giving the group position rather than one campus.

exceptions.messageShown: No chart of accounts has been set up. The books cannot be read until it exists.

exceptions.condition: The two columns do not agree
exceptions.systemResponse: The trial balance is still produced and the difference is shown prominently (BR-3).
exceptions.messageShown: The trial balance does not balance. Debits exceed credits by PKR 4,000.

exceptions.condition: The date range spans no posted entry
exceptions.systemResponse: The ledger shows its empty state with the opening balance, rather than a blank screen.
exceptions.messageShown: No entries in this period. The opening balance was PKR 148,200.

exceptions.condition: The date range is longer than the system will render at once
exceptions.systemResponse: It pages, and the running balance continues correctly across pages rather than restarting.

exceptions.condition: The source document has been deactivated
exceptions.systemResponse: The trace still reaches it, since an entry must always be explainable (BR-6).

exceptions.condition: A user attempts to post an entry from this screen
exceptions.systemResponse: There is no such control. Entries arrive from elsewhere (BR-4).

exceptions.condition: The trial balance is produced for a date before the financial year began
exceptions.systemResponse: It is refused rather than produced against an undefined opening position.
exceptions.messageShown: That date falls before the financial year begins.

departures.requirement: There is no route from any screen in this use case that creates, changes or deletes a ledger entry.
A trial balance across a full financial year of 200,000 entries is produced within 10 seconds.
Every entry resolves to its source document in at most two steps, and the trace survives the source being deactivated.
The running balance is continuous across pages and matches the closing balance exactly at the end of the range.
Ledger entries are retained 7 years and are never hard-deleted.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
